data.reasoning: The package contains standard AUR packaging files for an Electron application. The PKGBUILD fetches source from the official GitHub repository using a pinned tag and verifies checksums. Build steps are standard npm commands. The disagreement was solely caused by an API error in the first model when reviewing low-risk files (.gitignore and blockbench.desktop). The second model successfully reviewed these files and confirmed they are safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The first model (qwen) encountered HTTP 400 API errors when attempting to audit .gitignore and blockbench.desktop, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The second model (deepseek) successfully audited these files and found them to be standard, non-malicious configuration files.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to audit .gitignore and blockbench.desktop due to API errors (HTTP 400).
learnings: Implement retry logic for transient API errors (like HTTP 400) instead of immediately marking a file as inconclusive.

When calculating the final package verdict, weigh the risk of files that failed to audit. Failures on low-risk files (e.g., .gitignore, .desktop) should not necessarily force an inconclusive package verdict if the high-risk files (PKGBUILD, .install) are verified safe.
